R101.note: JNDI filter parameterization ({0}/{1} + filterArgs) is the correct RFC-2254-safe fix; no other behavior change.

R102.note: snprintf with size check replaces unbounded strcpy/strcat; disclosed rejection on overlong input matches the existing pattern already used for the output buffer.

R103.note: mysqli prepared statement preserves the original null/false-returning error contract.

R104.note: Primary fix (whitelist enforced inside the dynamic-SQL mapper) is self-contained and correct; the write-up also shows a second, alternative service-layer-only approach that is a bit confusingly juxtaposed but not itself wrong.

R105.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES) on both tainted fields, no other change.

R106.note: Strict fullmatch email regex blocks CRLF in the envelope commands; minor edge case is that a legitimate empty failed_sender would now raise instead of proceeding, but that's not the documented normal flow.

R107.note: resize() correctly gives the vector real size before indexed writes; behavior identical for count<=fields.size().

R108.note: firebase/php-jwt JWT::decode() with a Key performs real signature verification before trusting claims; failure path returns null as before.

R110.note: execFile with an argument array closes the reported shell-injection sink; a domain value starting with '-' could still be read as a whois flag (option injection), a distinct gap the write-up doesn't mention.

R111.note: AES-256-CBC with a real random IV correctly fixes the weak-cipher finding, but the response format changes silently from raw ciphertext to IV||ciphertext -- disclosed in the explanation, but it's an observable wire-format change any existing decrypting client would need to be updated for.

R112.note: Blade {!! !!} to {{ }} enables auto-escaping; nothing else touched.

R113.note: Adds same-origin host allowlist plus scheme check before sendRedirect; relative/local redirects still work.

R114.note: proc_open with an argument array removes shell interpretation for the reported sink; requestedName isn't basename()'d before being passed as an argument so a leading '-' could still be read as a flag by legacy-convert, a pre-existing gap not newly introduced.

R115.note: random_bytes(16)/bin2hex replaces uniqid(); correctly drops the attacker-influenced prefix.

R116.note: html.EscapeString on both fields; the local variable named 'html' only shadows the package after the declaration line so it still compiles and resolves correctly.

R117.note: Generic client message plus server-side logger.error preserves diagnosability while closing the info leak.

R118.note: escape-html applied to the actual tainted query param; unrelated server-controlled values left as-is.

R119.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes replaces seeded Random; dropping the seed query param is harmless since unbound query params are ignored by ASP.NET Core model binding.

R120.note: authorize() + ownership policy check is the standard Laravel fix; requirement to add the policy method is stated plainly.

R121.note: Full method rewritten with PreparedStatement including the declaration type change; compiles and preserves the finally-block cleanup.

R122.note: Fixed snippet keeps 'Statement sqlStatement' declared but calls sqlStatement.setString(...), which Statement does not define -- as written this does not compile.

R123.note: Type-asserts the signing method to *jwt.SigningMethodRSA} inside keyfunc, the documented mitigation for alg-confusion in golang-jwt.

R124.note: strnlen bounded to sizeof(record->name) stops the overread.

R125.note: Same case and same fix as R102: snprintf with bound check, consistent with existing error pattern.

R126.note: json_decode replaces unserialize, eliminating object-injection gadget surface; controller's array-subscript access is preserved.

R127.note: Adds segment.size() bound check alongside the existing claimedCapacity check; same silent-return shape as before.

R128.note: DOM construction with textContent/createTextNode reproduces the original visual structure while auto-escaping.

R129.note: secrets.randbelow(max-min+1)+min correctly preserves the original inclusive range semantics.

R130.note: Absolute-path/'..'-prefix rejection plus canonical containment check closes traversal while leaving in-directory access untouched.

R131.note: List-form subprocess.run without shell=True closes the reported shell injection; a filename starting with '-' could still be read as a libreoffice flag (option injection), not addressed but not newly introduced either.

R132.note: SecureRandom is a drop-in replacement for the same nextFloat() call site; output shape unchanged.

R133.note: SQL injection is closed, but the write-up's two edits are inconsistent: the fixed snippet introduces a new local 'preparedStatement' that is never closed, while the separately-suggested declaration rename targets the untouched 'sqlStatement' field -- applied together this leaks the real PreparedStatement in the finally block.

R134.note: The overflow guard 'count > Integer.MAX_VALUE / size' divides by size with no size==0 guard, but size==0 is a valid input per the existing bounds check -- that request now throws an uncaught ArithmeticException instead of returning the previously-valid empty buffer, and the explanation incorrectly claims this case is handled safely.

R137.note: Replacing exec() with Files.list() removes command execution entirely; neither version writes to the HTTP response, so external behavior is unchanged.

R138.note: offset>capacity || length>capacity-offset correctly bounds the write and avoids size_t underflow.

R139.note: crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('base64url') is a clean CSPRNG replacement used identically as a token/map key.
